title: Rigatoni with tomato & garlic
summary: A simple weeknight pasta, ready in 20 minutes. Great for the auto pasta timer.
source: Written for REMY by Claude, timers from cook-times.json. Waiting for Matthew's review.

steps.instruction: Fill a large pot with about 2 litres of water, cover it, and bring it to a rolling boil on high. Then add the salt.
looks_right: big bubbles breaking the surface all over
looks_wrong: only tiny bubbles on the bottom (not boiling yet)
a small pot with too little water
steps.done_when: The water is at a big rolling boil and salted.

steps.instruction: Tip in the rigatoni and stir straight away so it doesn't stick. The timer starts as soon as it goes in.
looks_right: pasta moving freely in the bubbling water
looks_wrong: pasta clumped together or stuck to the bottom
foam about to boil over (turn the heat down a little)
steps.done_when: The pasta is in, stirred and the timer is running. Remind the cook to check their packet time.

steps.instruction: While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a pan on medium-low and add the sliced garlic. Keep it gentle: garlic burns fast.
looks_right: garlic sizzling gently in the oil
garlic turning pale golden at the edges
looks_wrong: garlic going brown or black (it'll taste bitter: start again)
garlic frying hard and fast (heat too high: turn it down)
steps.done_when: The garlic is pale golden and smells sweet, about 1–2 minutes.

steps.instruction: Pour in the tomatoes and chilli flakes, add a pinch of salt, and let it bubble gently while the pasta finishes.
looks_right: the sauce thickening and turning a deeper red
looks_wrong: sauce catching and sticking on the bottom
steps.done_when: The sauce has thickened a little and no longer looks watery.

steps.instruction: When the pasta timer says check, taste a piece. It should be al dente: tender with a little bite. Scoop out a mug of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
looks_right: the bite shows no chalky white core
steps.done_when: The pasta passes the bite test and is drained, with a mug of pasta water saved. Ask the cook to bite a piece or hold one up to the camera.

steps.instruction: Tip the pasta into the sauce with a splash of the saved pasta water and toss well over the heat for a minute. Tear in the basil, taste, and season.
looks_right: glossy sauce clinging to every tube
looks_wrong: watery sauce pooling at the bottom (keep tossing over the heat)
dry, sticky pasta (add more pasta water)
steps.done_when: The pasta is glossy and coated. Serve with Parmesan on top.
